answerNotes.HOOK: A fishing hook catches by its pointed curve. A wall hook is shaped for hanging objects rather than catching fish.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.FORK: A fork's prongs hold pieces of food. A garden fork is a larger tool sharing that pronged shape.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.TOOL: A tool is an implement used to do a job. The clue may describe its action, such as cutting, turning, or gripping.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a line of things side by side. Garden plants, theater seats, and letters in a puzzle can all be arranged in rows.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.

answerNotes.GATE: A gate opens through a fence or other boundary. Hinges let it move, and a latch holds it closed.
answerNotes.SCREW: A screw has a spiral thread. Turning it moves it into material; a nail is usually driven with a hammer instead.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.LEVEL: A level checks whether a surface is horizontal or vertical. It helps a frame hang straight without judging by sight alone.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.FENCE: A fence marks a boundary or encloses an area. The gate is its movable entrance rather than another name for the whole barrier.
answerNotes.PAINT: Paint leaves a colored coating on a surface. A stain usually allows more of wood's natural grain to remain visible.

answerNotes.BARREL: A barrel is a large rounded container. A rain barrel collects runoff; its tap lets water leave without lifting the whole container.
answerNotes.RAIN: Rain is liquid water falling from clouds. Snow and hail reach the ground in solid forms instead.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.TAP: Tap can mean a faucet or a light knock. The water-container scene uses the faucet meaning.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.SCREEN: Screen can mean a display surface or a mesh barrier. The phone and movie scenes use the display meaning; a porch door uses the mesh meaning.

answerNotes.PALM: Palm can mean a tree or the inside of a hand. In the entry-to-Jerusalem story, it is the tree whose branches are carried.
answerNotes.COTTON: Cotton is a plant fiber used in many washable household items. Wool instead comes from an animal's fleece.
answerNotes.HAND: Hand can name a body part or a clock pointer. A clock's minute hand makes a full turn each hour.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.SEAM: A seam joins pieces of fabric. A hem finishes an edge instead of joining two separate pieces.

answerNotes.LEVEL: A level checks whether a surface is horizontal or vertical. It helps a frame hang straight without judging by sight alone.
answerNotes.GREEN: Green describes many growing leaves. It is also a color name in its own right, so read whether the clue asks for a plant or its appearance.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.BRANCH: A branch is a woody limb extending from a tree or shrub. A twig is usually a smaller, thinner piece of that growth.
answerNotes.CUT: Cut is an action, unlike a tool name such as scissors or knife. Matching the clue's part of speech helps narrow the answer.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.
